expectations.text: Repository left unmodified (work done on copies)
Every source paragraph translated (Arabic paragraphs >= 85% of source paragraphs)
Translation body is Arabic (English words under 5% of words, note excluded)
Register is colloquial Levantine suitable for a blog, not MSA
expectations.evidence: Clearly Levantine (Jordanian) throughout: «خلّينا نقول حدا قلّي», «ولا بقدر ألفّ», «فبرنّ على ألبرتو», «هسا صرت أعرف», «بس مش متأكد مية بالمية», «عم يقطع ساحة نافونا بهاللحظة بالزبط», «رح أصير أثق فيه أقل».

expectations.text: Jokes land in Arabic (the penguin / Navona joke and 'He laughs' kept as jokes, not flattened or explained)
expectations.evidence: «بيضحك.» kept as its own one-word paragraph; penguin/Navona joke kept dry: «وممكن يكون في بطريق هربان عم يقطع ساحة نافونا بهاللحظة بالزبط ويخرّبلي المثال». The whales line lands too: «ويلزقوها على الحيتان، بس لأنه نفس الثمّ اللي عم يحكي».

expectations.text: Faithful: no content cut or added compared with the English section
expectations.evidence: All 7 source paragraphs present with the same content; the only addition is the connective «هسا» before 'I know more...', which the note discloses. Technical terms kept in English (metadata, ranking systems, machine learning) per blog style.

expectations.text: Translation text adds no explanation of jokes, seeds or references
expectations.evidence: Translation body contains no glosses or explanations; the note mentions «سلسلة الثقة» points back to the previous section but suggests the author decide, rather than adding it to the text.

expectations.text: Note is short and actionable (lists the few choices the author should check)
expectations.evidence: Note has a 'To check' line with concrete choices («ساحة نافونا» vs «بياتسا نافونا», «عشت فيه» vs «عايش فيه», whether to keep 'about Jordan') plus a standalone-context warning. It runs a bit long (commit hash, ar_register.py stats), but the actionable items are easy to find.

notes: Lively, natural Jordanian blog Arabic that keeps the timing of the jokes. The note is in English and tagged 'remove before posting', which suits the author. Minor: «الثمّ» is a nice colloquial touch; the note could drop the tool statistics.
